subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK/embedding fit
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenora.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@zenora.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK/embedding fit

Alex / Sanjay —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Pain points you shared
- High per-query cost on your embeddings + reranking pipeline (esp. peak hours)
- Latency spikes when serving short multi-turn chats (p95 > 400ms)
- Need for structured outputs and deterministic function-calling for data enrichment flows

Goals we heard
- Reduce per-query cost ~2.5–3x for embeddings + rerank workload
- Improve chat p95 to sub-200ms for common request sizes
- Ship a reliable, auditable pipeline with function-calling and structured outputs for downstream systems

Integration / fit notes
- Redwood can support your embedding + rerank pipeline via our streaming embeddings API + on-the-fly reranking (we discussed prefix caching to lower token costs).
- SDK change required: minor client update to use our embeddings batching endpoint and enable function-calling hooks (we’ll share snippets).
- Structured outputs: suggest using our JSON schema enforcement + function-calling for the enrichment step to ensure deterministic fields.

Open technical items we promised to follow up on
- Example latency and cost numbers for a 32-token embedding + 512-token rerank scenario (we’ll provide per-1000-query cost and p50/p95).
- Data residency / retention details and SOC2 artifacts (attached Q&A).
- Quick demo focusing on embedding accuracy and rerank throughput with your sample dataset.

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive next week with Michael (our solutions engineer) to run a short demo and look at your sample traces.
2) We’ll send a draft proposal and TCO estimate (attachment) with a couple of deployment options (hosted vs dedicated).
3) Once you give us a preferred date for the demo, we’ll provision a short trial environment and run a quick smoke test with your sample queries.

Attachments: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf (PDF, 320KB); zenora-data-retention-qna.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)

Thanks again — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenora.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@zenora.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK/embedding fit

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A couple of quick clarifying questions before we lock the demo time: 

1) Timeline: we’re aiming to have a proof-of-concept run in the next 3 weeks. Can you confirm Michael’s availability week of Jun 14?
2) Hybrid support: we have some sensitive workloads that may need to stay on-prem — does Redwood support a hybrid setup where embeddings run on dedicated private deployment and rerank on hosted?
3) Can you also share approximate baseline numbers for a 32-token embedding + 512-token rerank (p50/p95 latency and per-1k cost) so our infra team can do a quick budget check?

On the demo: we’ll provide a small sample dataset (500 queries) and an example rerank set. Looking forward to the proposal.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Senior Product Manager, Zenora
alex.chen@zenora.com | (510) 555-0199

Michael / Vivek — forwarding Zenora’s reply and the recap. They’re targeting a PoC in ~3 weeks and asked for:
- Demo week of Jun 14 (can you confirm availability?)
- Baseline latency + cost numbers for 32-token embed + 512-token rerank (p50/p95 and per-1k cost)
- A short plan to show how a hybrid deployment would work (hosted rerank + private embeddings) — they want to keep some data on-prem.

Michael: can you own the demo + quick cost estimate? I’d like a 30–40 minute demo that shows:
- Embedding throughput/latency with our streaming SDK and batching enabled
- Rerank latency at 100QPS and how prefix caching saves tokens
- Example function-calling + structured JSON output that their enrichment service can ingest

Please prepare:
- 1 slide with the demo agenda
- 1 table with cost comparatives (hosted vs dedicated vs hybrid) for the 1k-query profile
- A short script and example commands we’ll run against their sample dataset

CC’ing Vivek to confirm commercial guardrails we can offer for the PoC (credits / trial size).

Thanks — let me know if you want to sync quick before Monday.

Best,
Marissa

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 18:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK/embedding fit

Marissa — happy to take this. Quick plan: 

1) Demo availability: I’m free Jun 15 or Jun 16 afternoons PT; can do Jun 14 morning if preferred.
2) Baseline numbers (estimate for the PoC profile):
   - 32-token embedding (streaming, batch size 16): p50 ~22ms, p95 ~65ms per embedding; cost ~ $0.30 per 1k (hosted, optimized cache)
   - 512-token rerank (single-pass scoring, batching): p50 ~48ms, p95 ~180ms; cost ~ $1.10 per 1k
   - Combined profile (embed + rerank): p50 ~75ms, p95 ~245ms; combined cost ~ $1.40 per 1k queries
   - With dedicated pooling + quantization, we estimate ~2.5x cost savings and p95 down to ~160–180ms in most cases.
3) Hybrid: supported. We’ll propose a hybrid architecture doc (short) that pins embeddings to a private cluster and routes rerank to hosted instances with encrypted transport. I’ll attach a one-pager and demo script before Monday.

I’ll prepare: slide agenda, cost table, demo script, and a short hybrid architecture diagram (attachment stub). Planning to circulate by EOD Monday.

—Michael

Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
